env.docs: Verbosity, as `tracing` directives such as `info` or `tankovault_api=debug,info`. Read by `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env`, which is consulted *before* `telemetry.log_filter` and wins over it when set.
env.name: RUST_LOG

enabled.description: Write audit records. `false` installs a sink that discards them.

record_ip.description: Record the client IP. Off by default, since an IP is personal data under GDPR Art. 4(1).

record_user_agent.description: Record the client `User-Agent` alongside each event.

retention_days.description:
Days to retain audit records before the sweep deletes them. `0` disables the sweep, which
GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), storage limitation, rarely allows.

sweep_interval_hours.description: Hours between retention sweeps. Ignored when [`Self::retention_days`] is `0`.

access_ttl_minutes.description:
How long an access token stays valid. Short, because nothing revokes one before it
expires; the refresh token is the revocable half.

cookie_secure.description:
Marks the refresh cookie `Secure`.

Defaults to true: a `bool`'s implicit default is `false`, which would silently send a
30-day refresh credential over plain HTTP.

Also selects the cookie's name/path (`__Host-` vs unprefixed), since a `__Host-`
cookie without `Secure` is refused by the browser. Flipping this forces one re-login.

jwt_secret.description:
HS256 signing key for access tokens; wrapped in `SecretString` so a `tracing::debug!(?cfg)`
on this Debug-deriving, nested struct can't publish the key that authenticates every
session.

mfa_challenge_ttl_minutes.description:
How long a half-finished sign-in (password accepted, second factor still owed) may
sit before the user has to start again.

mfa_encryption_key.description:
Base64 (standard alphabet) 32-byte key that seals TOTP secrets at rest.

Deliberately *not* derived from [`Self::jwt_secret`]: rotating the signing key is a
routine operation, and deriving from it would silently invalidate every enrolled
authenticator app, the same class of failure as rotating `password_pepper` and
stranding the seeded admin. Unset disables TOTP enrolment only; security keys and
recovery codes are unaffected, since neither stores a symmetric secret.

refresh_ttl_days.description:
How long a refresh token stays valid, and so how long a signed-out-of-sight session can
come back. Each use rotates the token and revokes its predecessor.

step_up_max_ttl_minutes.description:
The ceiling on that sliding: the longest an elevation is honoured after it was earned,
however continuously it is used.

step_up_ttl_minutes.description:
How long a step-up elevation survives **unused** before a sensitive action prompts again.
Every elevated request slides it forward.

totp_issuer.description:
The issuer name an authenticator app files the entry under. Defaults to
[`Self::webauthn_rp_name`], then to the product name: one label for both prompts.

webauthn_origin.description:
Public origin of the web app, for passkeys, such as `https://tanko.example.com`.

Cannot be inferred from a request: `Host` is attacker-controlled, and trusting it
would let anyone mint credentials under a domain of their choosing. Unset falls back
to [`tankovault_config::EmailConfig::base_url`] and disables only passkeys.

webauthn_rp_id.description:
Relying-party id: the registrable domain credentials are bound to. Defaults to
[`Self::webauthn_origin`]'s host. Set to a parent domain only if the app moves between
subdomains and keys must survive the move.

webauthn_rp_name.description: The name the authenticator shows in its prompt ("Save a passkey for …"); purely cosmetic.

bind_addr.description:
The public listener. Everything a reader's browser and the native client reach is
served from here, behind whatever terminates TLS.

bot_user_agent.description:
The identifiable crawler user-agent, applied to any provider still carrying the built-in
default. A provider whose politeness names its own user-agent keeps it.

notice.description:
The whole notice, verbatim, when the `© {year} {holder}` shape does not fit. Wins over
both fields above and over the catalogue's translation of the line.

year.description: The year, or a range (`2024–2026`). Unset is the current year at request time.

url.description:
Where the label links. Unset renders the label as plain text, for a deployment with no
public licence page.

name.description:
The product name as prose uses it: email subjects and bodies, page titles, the
authenticator prompt and the desktop connect screen.

project_url.description: Where the project lives, linked from the footer and the desktop About tab.

releases_url.description: Where a reader downloads the native client.

tagline.description:
One line under the wordmark. Unset keeps the shipped, translated tagline. Set, it replaces
the tagline with this string in every language.

accent.description: The part drawn in the accent colour. Absent draws the lockup as one word.

lead.description: The part drawn in the body colour.

max_version.description:
The newest client version this deployment supports. Unset means the running service's own
version, since client and server are released together at one version.

min_version.description: The oldest client version this deployment supports. Unset means no floor.

release_repo.description:
The GitHub repository, as `owner/name`, that the native client reads its releases from.

Blank publishes none, and a client then keeps whichever repository it was built with.
A fork that ships its own signed installers names itself here.

control_plane_url.description:
Where the admin console's scan triggers and flag writes are forwarded, no trailing
slash. Every call to it carries the shared internal secret.

acquire_timeout_secs.description: How long a caller waits for a pooled connection before failing, in seconds.

max_connections.description: Upper bound on the connection pool.

base_url.description:
Public base URL of the web app, for absolute links in email such as the password-reset
link. No trailing slash.

envelope_from.description:
SMTP envelope sender (`MAIL FROM`), which can differ from the visible [`Self::from`]
header.

Providers enforcing "send as" checks, such as OVH Exchange, reject a mismatched envelope
sender, so unset means [`Self::username`].

from.description: Default `From` mailbox, such as `TankoVault <no-reply@example.com>`. Required to send.

host.description: SMTP host (OVH Exchange: `pro3.mail.ovh.net` for STARTTLS or `ssl0.ovh.net` for TLS).

port.description:
SMTP port. Unset, it follows [`Self::security`]: 465 for `tls`, 587 for `starttls`, 25
for `none`.

security.description: Transport security to use with the explicit host/port fields.

url.description: Full lettre relay URL. When set, it wins over the explicit fields below.

username.description: Login username. For OVH Exchange it is the full mailbox address.

refresh_secs.description:
Seconds between refreshes of a service's cached flag snapshot. It is how long a change
takes to reach the other replicas; the replica that served the change applies it at once.

name.description: The name peers know this service by, matching the key they list it under.

token.description:
Presented to peers under `identity = "token"`. Ignored under `mtls`, where the client
certificate is the credential.

san.description:
The client-certificate subject alternative name this peer presents under
`identity = "mtls"`, such as `api.tankovault.svc`.

token.description: The token this peer presents under `identity = "token"`.

peers.description: Which services may call this one, keyed by caller name.

ca.description: PEM bundle of the authorities a peer certificate must chain to.

cert.description: PEM certificate chain this service serves and presents.

probe_listen.description:
Address the credential-free `/health` and `/ready` probes bind to, in **plaintext**, on
their own listener (default `0.0.0.0:9091`). Read under `mtls` only.

An orchestrator probe presents no client certificate, so on the mTLS port its plain `GET`
gets a TLS alert and the replica is restarted as unhealthy. Set it to `null`, which drops
the listener, only where the prober can present a certificate.

token.description: Refused at boot. [`InternalAuthConfig::resolve`] names the per-caller keys that replace it.

default_locale.description:
Locale served when neither the request nor its `Accept-Language` header matches a
published one, for example `en`. Without it, the first published locale in alphabetical
order is served.

body.description:
Markdown text per locale, keyed by locale (`en`, `de-AT`). Usually supplied through a
`…__BODY__<LOCALE>_FILE` variable naming a mounted file. Each text is at most 1 MiB.
Exclusive with `url`.

order.description: Position in the index, lowest first. Documents with the same value are ordered by slug.

title.description: Display title per locale, keyed like `body`.

url.description:
Absolute `http` or `https` URL of a document hosted elsewhere, without credentials.
Exclusive with `body`.

documents.description:
The published documents, keyed by the slug their URL uses. A slug is lowercase letters,
digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, and starts with a letter or a digit.

adult_tags.description:
Additional genre chips that classify a series as adult, matched on their slug.

These add to the shipped terms in [`tankovault_domain::AdultTagSet`], and no switch drops
them. An emptied classifier would stop classifying silently, while the two supported ways
to show adult content, the deployment flag and the per-reader opt-in, both record a
decision.

enabled.description:
Install the Prometheus recorder and serve the scrape endpoint. When `false` the
scrape route answers `404` and no measurements are retained.

http_requests.description:
Also record per-request HTTP metrics. The request histogram is the expensive,
high-cardinality part, so it has its own switch.

listen.description:
Address the scrape endpoint binds on its **own** listener, apart from the service's
public port (default `0.0.0.0:9090`). `null` serves it on the primary port.

route.description: Path the scrape endpoint is mounted at.

events_max_age_secs.description: Longest the events stream keeps an event no consumer has acked, in seconds.

url.description: The connection URL, such as `nats://nats:4222` or `nats://user:pass@host`.

burst.description: The most requests a client may spend back-to-back.

per_minute.description: Sustained requests allowed per minute per client key, which is the bucket's refill rate.

enabled.description: Enforce limits. When `false` the layer is not mounted and costs nothing per request.

burst.description: The most requests a client may spend back-to-back.

per_minute.description: Sustained requests allowed per minute per client key, which is the bucket's refill rate.

burst.description: The most requests a client may spend back-to-back.

per_minute.description: Sustained requests allowed per minute per client key, which is the bucket's refill rate.

trust_forwarded_for.description:
Take the client key from `X-Forwarded-For` or `X-Real-IP`. Enable it **only behind a
reverse proxy that overwrites both**; otherwise any client forges a fresh key and bypasses
the limiter.

url.description: The connection URL, such as `redis://redis:6379` or `redis://:password@host`.

allow_credentials.description:
Allow credentialed cross-origin requests, carrying cookies or `Authorization`. Cannot be
combined with a wildcard origin.

allowed_origins.description: Exact origins allowed, such as `https://app.example.com`. Empty disables CORS.

expose_api_docs.description:
Serve the browsable API docs (`/scalar`) and the `OpenAPI` document.

Off by default in production and on elsewhere. Left on in production, it gives an
attacker every `/v1/admin/*` path, the permission vocabulary and the exact request bodies
without a failed probe.

hsts.description: Emit `Strict-Transport-Security`. Browsers ignore it over plain HTTP.

hsts_max_age_secs.description: `max-age` for the HSTS header, in seconds. The default is two years, the preload minimum.

max_body_bytes.description: Reject request bodies larger than this, in bytes, before they are buffered.

request_timeout_secs.description: Abort a request that has not produced a response within this many seconds.

security_headers.description:
Send the baseline set of hardening headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`,
`X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`).

trust_request_id.description:
Accept an inbound `X-Request-Id` instead of minting one. Enable it only behind a trusted
proxy, since a client-supplied id can poison log correlation.

admin_max_connections.description: Connections the admin pool may hold, on top of `database.max_connections`.

admin_secs.description:
Seconds one statement may run on a `/v1/admin` route or in the API's background sweeps.
`0` removes the ceiling.

interactive_secs.description:
Seconds one statement may run on every non-admin route: `/v1/me`, the public catalogue and
sign-in. `0` removes the ceiling.

sync_url.description: Where the `/v1/me/sync/*` proxies forward to, no trailing slash.

json_logs.description: Emit structured JSON logs, for production, in place of the human-readable format.

log_filter.description: `tracing` filter directives, such as `info,tankovault=debug`. `RUST_LOG` wins when set.

attach_stacktraces.description: Attach a stack trace to events that carry none of their own.

breadcrumb_level.description:
Least severe `tracing` level kept as a **breadcrumb**, the trail attached to the next
issue. Records at or above [`Self::capture_level`] become issues instead.

capture_level.description: Least severe `tracing` level reported as a Sentry **issue**.

debug.description: Print the SDK's own diagnostics to stderr, to prove a DSN works.

dsn.description:
Ingest URL, `https://<key>@<host>/<project>`.

Required while [`Self::enabled`] is set.

enabled.description:
Initialise the Sentry client. `false` installs no client, no panic hook and no layer,
so every other key here is inert and nothing is sent anywhere.

environment.description:
Environment tag on every event. Defaults to `production` under
`TANKOVAULT_PROFILE=production` and `development` otherwise.

http_transactions.description:
Record one Sentry transaction per request through the shared HTTP stack, named by the
matched route, so an id in the path does not become a transaction name.

[`Self::traces_sample_rate`] decides whether a transaction is kept. Off, the HTTP layer
starts no transactions; a broker delivery still starts one through the `tracing` layer.

max_breadcrumbs.description: How many breadcrumbs one event carries.

release.description:
Release tag on every event. Unset, it is the workspace version the binary was built
from, which ties an issue to a deploy.

sample_rate.description:
Fraction of captured events sent, `0.0`-`1.0`, decided at random per event. A lower rate
undercounts every issue and can miss a rare one entirely, so leave it at `1.0` unless
quota forces it lower.

send_default_pii.description:
Send personally identifying data with every event: the client IP, the full request
header set (`Authorization` and `Cookie` included) and the resolved user.

**Off, and worth leaving off.** A crash report does not need a reader's IP address or
session cookie, and Sentry is a third party under the deployment's data policy. On, it
also stops `sentry-tower` redacting sensitive headers in the HTTP middleware.

server_name.description: Host tag on every event. Unset, Sentry reports none.

shutdown_timeout_secs.description: How long process exit waits for queued events to drain.

span_attributes.description:
Copy `tracing` span fields onto the Sentry span as attributes. Off by default, because span
fields carry ids and user-supplied titles and a transaction is kept longer than a log line.

traces_sample_rate.description:
Fraction of traces this service **starts** that are recorded, `0.0`-`1.0`.

`0.0`, the default, starts none. The service still continues a trace that arrives already
sampled on a request or a broker message. Set the same rate on every service, since the
service that starts a trace decides whether it exists; `0.05`-`0.2` is an ordinary
production figure.

service_name.description: Service name reported in traces and metrics.

worker_url.description: Where the admin console's provider dry-run is forwarded, no trailing slash.

keys.docs: The connection URL, such as `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/tankovault`.
Upper bound on the connection pool.
How long a caller waits for a pooled connection before failing, in seconds.

sign-in. `0` removes the ceiling.
